content.text: Preserve's server spans return 500, and most of its failures are outgoing POST client spans with no HTTP status, so the failing call is likely a connection-level error. I'll check the preserve logs and which POST targets fail.

content.text: The failing call is preserve's POST to ts-travel-service `trip_detail`, which ends with "Unexpected end of file from server". I'll compare ts-travel-service's own spans between periods to see whether the travel side or the calling side is altered.

content.text: The hubble metrics do show a drop counter on the preserve pod in the abnormal period. I'll compare drops and HTTP request counts for the preserve and travel pods across both periods.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, metric, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*) n, round(sum(value),1) total FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric IN ('hubble_drop_total','hubble_http_requests_total','hubble_icmp_total') AND (attr_source LIKE '%preserve%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%preserve%' OR attr_source LIKE '%travel-service%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%travel-service%' OR attr_source LIKE '%security%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%contacts%') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm' p, metric, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*) n, round(sum(value),1) total FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric IN ('hubble_drop_total','hubble_http_requests_total','hubble_icmp_total') AND (attr_source LIKE '%preserve%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%preserve%' OR attr_source LIKE '%travel-service%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%travel-service%' OR attr_source LIKE '%security%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%contacts%') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,4,1 LIMIT 60

content.text: Drops on the preserve pod appear only in the abnormal period (48 total). I'll line up per-minute failed preserve→travel calls against the drop counter and the travel-plan/route-plan path to see whether they start together.

input.query: SELECT date_trunc('minute', time) m, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-preserve-service' AND attr_span_kind='Client' AND span_name='POST' AND attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) failed_post, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-preserve-service' AND attr_span_kind='Client' AND span_name='POST' AND attr_status_code<>'Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ok_post, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-preserve-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) preserve_srv, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-route-plan-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) rp_srv, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-travel-plan-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) tp_srv FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT date_trunc('minute', time) m, sum(CASE WHEN metric='hubble_drop_total' THEN value ELSE 0 END) drops, count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN metric='hubble_drop_total' THEN attr_source END) drop_src FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: The failed preserve→travel POSTs are concentrated in the same minutes as the preserve errors, starting at minute 2 of the window. Drop counters are spread across many pods, so I need the normal-period baseline before reading them as a signal.

input.query: SELECT 'norm' p, attr_source, count(*) n, round(sum(value),1) total FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric='hubble_drop_total' GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'abn' p, attr_source, count(*) n, round(sum(value),1) total FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric='hubble_drop_total' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1
SELECT service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, attr_span_kind, span_name, count(*) n FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name LIKE '%trip_detail%' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 20

content.text: Drop counters show up across many pods in both periods, so they're background noise and not a signal for this fault. Next I'll check who calls ts-travel-service's `trip_detail` successfully and whether any travel spans attach to preserve's failing POSTs.

input.query: SELECT p.service_name parent_svc, p.span_name parent_span, c.service_name, c.span_name, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50ms, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50 FROM abnormal_traces c LEFT JOIN abnormal_traces p ON c.parent_span_id=p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE c.span_name LIKE '%trip_detail%' AND c.attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 20

SELECT p.service_name parent_svc, p.span_name parent_span, c.service_name, c.span_name, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50ms FROM normal_traces c LEFT JOIN normal_traces p ON c.parent_span_id=p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE c.span_name LIKE '%trip_detail%' AND c.attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 20

content.text: This resolves the direction of the fault. Every failing preserve POST has a matching travel server span that returned 200 with normal timing, so travel completed the work and the connection was cut on the way back to preserve. That points to an HTTP-layer abort at the caller, not a network fault. Next I'll check whether the route-plan and travel-plan latency rises are a separate fault or just knock-on effects.

input.query: SELECT service_name, 'abn' p, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95 FROM abnormal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Server' AND service_name IN ('ts-route-plan-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-travel2-service','ts-travel-service','ts-route-service','ts-seat-service','ts-basic-service','ts-ui-dashboard','ts-train-service','ts-station-service','ts-contacts-service','ts-price-service') GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT service_name, 'norm' p, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95 FROM normal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Server' AND service_name IN ('ts-route-plan-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-travel2-service','ts-travel-service','ts-route-service','ts-seat-service','ts-basic-service','ts-ui-dashboard','ts-train-service','ts-station-service','ts-contacts-service','ts-price-service') GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

SELECT service_name, span_name, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM abnormal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Server' AND service_name IN ('ts-route-plan-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-ui-dashboard') GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,3 DESC

content.text: Route-plan and travel-plan have very few spans in both periods, and their slow trip-planning calls exist in normal too, so they look like workload noise rather than a second fault. The last thing to confirm is that preserve's failures reach ts-ui-dashboard.

input.query: SELECT c.service_name caller, c.span_name, c.attr_span_kind, p.service_name parent_svc, p.span_name parent_span, p.attr_status_code parent_status, p.attr_http_response_status_code parent_code, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50ms FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces p ON c.parent_span_id=p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE p.service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND c.service_name='ts-preserve-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 20

SELECT service_name, span_name, attr_http_response_status_code code, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND attr_status_code='Error' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 10
